title: Security essentials
summary: Injection, secrets, dependency risk, safe headers, authentication tokens and denial of service in Node services.

sections.title: Injection
sections.body: Anything built from user input and then interpreted is a risk: SQL, shell commands, HTML, file paths, regular expressions. Use parameterised queries (`WHERE id = $1`), argument arrays for child processes, output escaping in templates, and validated paths. In MongoDB-style queries, reject objects where you expect strings, or `{"$gt": ""}` can match everything.

sections.title: Prototype pollution
sections.body: Merging untrusted JSON into objects can set `__proto__` and change `Object.prototype` for the whole process, so every object suddenly has `isAdmin: true`. Validate input against a schema, skip `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` keys in merge helpers, and use `Object.create(null)` or `Map` for dictionaries keyed by user data.

sections.title: Auth tokens and sessions
sections.body: Hash passwords with a slow algorithm (`scrypt`, `argon2` or `bcrypt`), never a plain hash. Signed tokens such as JWTs must be verified with a pinned algorithm, checked for expiry and audience, and kept short-lived. Cookies carrying sessions should be `HttpOnly`, `Secure` and `SameSite`. Compare secrets with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.

sections.title: Dependencies and denial of service
sections.body:
Most of your code is dependencies. Commit the lockfile, install with `npm ci`, run `npm audit` in CI, review new packages and avoid running install scripts you do not need.

Denial of service is easy in a single-threaded server: cap body sizes, set timeouts, rate-limit, and beware regular expressions with nested quantifiers like `(a+)+$`, which can take exponential time on crafted input (ReDoS).

pitfalls: Building SQL or shell commands with template strings.
Deep-merging request bodies into config or user objects.
Accepting the algorithm named in a JWT header, including `none`.
No body size limit or request timeout.

gotchas.question: Why is `JSON.parse` of untrusted input not enough to be safe?
gotchas.answer: Parsing is safe, but the result can contain keys such as `__proto__` and unexpected types such as objects where you expected strings. What you do next (merging, querying, rendering) is where the attack happens, so validate the parsed value against a schema.

gotchas.question: What security headers would you set on a JSON API?
gotchas.answer: `Strict-Transport-Security` to force HTTPS, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, a restrictive `Content-Security-Policy` if any HTML is served, CORS headers that list exact allowed origins, and no `X-Powered-By`. Middleware such as helmet sets sensible defaults.

gotchas.question: What is ReDoS?
gotchas.answer: Regular expression denial of service: a pattern with ambiguous nested repetition backtracks exponentially on certain inputs, freezing the event loop. Simplify the pattern, limit input length, or use a linear-time regex engine.
